capabilities: Custom 4-layer PCB with STM32H743 MCU, TMC5160 closed-loop stepper drivers, and isolated digital I/O for limit switches and relays
Real-time firmware running FreeRTOS with a dedicated motion planning task at 40kHz step generation using Bresenham interpolation with look-ahead acceleration profiling
gRPC bi-directional streaming API for toolpath upload, real-time position feedback, and parameter adjustment without pausing operations
Web-based dashboard with live 3D toolpath preview, axis position readout, speed override, and job queue management
Automatic calibration routine using limit switch homing and probe-based tool length offset measurement with 0.01mm repeatability
architecture: Firmware architecture follows a three-layer design: a hardware abstraction layer (HAL) wrapping TIM peripherals, GPIO, and DMA for step generation; a motion planning layer implementing a look-ahead acceleration planner with trapezoidal velocity profiles and corner rounding; and a command layer that parses buffered G-code blocks into the planner's internal trajectory queue. The planner runs at 1kHz, outputting position setpoints to the step generation ISR running at 40kHz via a double-buffered pipeline.

data.title: Tunpy
data.description: An adapted version of the Thonny IDE with a custom Python language interpreter

introduction:
We all know the 'repeat ... until' loop in algorithmic learning.

The Tunisian algorithms curriculum in secondary schools uses it despite the use of python as the main programming language. And, python doesn't have that loop in its syntax.

As a turnaround, the teachers used the 'while not' syntax which is algorimically wrong. And what make it harder to correctly emulate the behaviour of the repeat loop is that the use of the keyword break is forbidden inside code blocks.

Tunpy comes with a simple idea; add the 'repeat ... until' loop to the python syntax.

As a result the below syntax is born:

dorepeat:

instructions

upuntil exit_condition

Also, Tunpy comes packed with all the necessary libraries used in the curriculum.

capabilities: Correctly write the repeat loop while preserving the python syntax philosophy.
Natively integrate all libraries used in the curriculum.
Natively integrate the 'Ajouter le code Qt5' plugin used by scientific students when using Qt5 interfaces.
Continuous maintenaince according to Thonny versionning.
French as a default language.
Bug report to me@ahmedev.com
